# Dopplr

> Dopplr shows each shopper how a specific garment fits her own body on the product page, built per category. Innerwear (bras and intimate apparel) is live with brands including Jockey and Enamor; dresswear is in early access. Shoppers enter a few measurements; no photos and no camera.

Dopplr (by Highstreet 3D, Inc.) is a privacy-first alternative to image-based virtual try-on and to generic size-recommendation tools, built for fit-sensitive categories, starting with bras and intimate apparel and now dresses. Where most tools either render a photo or predict a size from body data, Dopplr models the garment itself, so it answers how a specific style will fit a specific body.

## Key facts
- Category: fit intelligence / fit technology for ecommerce; a virtual try-on alternative and size-recommendation alternative for innerwear and dresswear
- Built for: innerwear (minimiser, sports and everyday bras), live; dresswear (hem position by height, fit by body shape), early access
- Pricing: innerwear pilots at $40 per style per month, typically starting with the top 20 styles
- How it works: models garment construction (band, cup, wire, coverage, fabric behavior) together with a shopper's measurements and bust shape to produce a personalized fit answer on the product page
- Privacy: no photos, no camera, no biometric data; measurements only
- Outcomes (innerwear, Enamor deployment): 19% first-time-buyer conversion lift and 3.5x product-page engagement (observed); 17% fewer fit-related returns (modeled). No dresswear results yet.
- Platforms: Shopify app (installed via a private link), Salesforce Commerce Cloud, or any product page via a lightweight JS embed
- Compared to: True Fit, Fit Analytics, EyeFitU, 3DLOOK, SAIZ (size recommendation); WEARFITS, Sizer, NetVirta, image-based virtual try-on; Brarista (lingerie fit). Dopplr's difference is garment-construction modeling and a no-photo, on-PDP fit answer purpose-built for intimate apparel.
